keys that change how Claude Code behaves: which model it starts with, what it can run without asking, which files it can’t read, how it looks in your terminal, and what your organization enforces.</span>

[&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-green-800 dark:text-green-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">To look up a specific key, go to <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-reference">All settings</a>, which lists every key with the file you set it in, its default, and an example.</span></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code reads settings from JSON settings files such as <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>. It looks for them in a few locations, and <a class="link" href="#settings-files-and-who-they-affect">the file it reads a setting from decides who the setting applies to</a>. This page covers those files: which one to put a setting in, how to change a setting and confirm it applied, and which value Claude Code uses when the same key is set in more than one file. <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions">Configure permissions</a> covers what Claude Code can run without asking and how to write <code>allow</code>, <code>ask</code>, and <code>deny</code> rules.</span>
<div aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note" role="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path clip-rule="evenodd" d="M 9 1.6714 C 13.0371 1.6714 16.3286 4.9629 16.3286 9 C 16.3286 13.0371 13.0371 16.3286 9 16.3286 C 7.0574 16.3252 5.1953 15.552 3.8217 14.1783 C 2.448 12.8047 1.6748 10.9426 1.6714 9 C 1.6714 4.9629 4.9629 1.6714 9 1.6714 Z M 9 0 C 4.0371 0 0 4.0371 0 9 C 0 13.9629 4.0371 18 9 18 C 13.9629 18 18 13.9629 18 9 C 18 4.0371 13.9629 0 9 0 Z M 10.2857 3.8571 H 7.7143 V 10.2857 H 10.2857 V 3.8571 Z M 10.2857 11.5714 H 7.7143 V 14.1429 H 10.2857 V 11.5714 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-rule="evenodd" stroke="none"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">This page covers Claude Code running on your machine: the terminal, the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/vs-code">VS Code</a> and <a class="link" href="/docs/en/jetbrains">JetBrains</a> extensions, and the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop">desktop app</a>, which all read the same settings files. A <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web">cloud session</a> runs on a different machine and reads only some of them; see <a class="link" href="#settings-in-cloud-sessions">Settings in cloud sessions</a>.</span></div></div>

<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="settings-files-and-who-they-affect"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#settings-files-and-who-they-affect">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Settings files and who they affect</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code reads settings from four files, and an organization can also deliver managed settings from the claude.ai console. Each source has a scope: the set of people and projects a setting saved in it applies to, whether that’s just you, everyone in a project, or everyone in your organization.</span>
<!-- --><div class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px"><div aria-label="Scrollable table" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" data-id="base-ui-_R_3cllktbsnlhjiuqsnpfiutb_-viewport" role="region" style="overflow:scroll" tabindex="-1"><div class="flex" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px]"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left">Scope</th><th style="text-align:left">File</th><th style="text-align:left">Who it affects</th><th style="text-align:left">Use it for</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left">User</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>~/.claude/settings.json</code></td><td style="text-align:left">You, in every project on this machine</td><td style="text-align:left">Personal preferences: theme, editor mode, default model, your own permission rules</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Shared project</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>.claude/settings.json</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Everyone working in the folder that contains it. In a git repository, commit it so teammates get it</td><td style="text-align:left">Team permissions, hooks, plugins, and the environment variables the project needs</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Project local</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>.claude/settings.local.json</code></td><td style="text-align:left">You, in this one project only. Claude Code keeps it out of git when it creates the file; if you create it by hand, add it to <code>.gitignore</code> yourself</td><td style="text-align:left">Personal overrides for one project, and testing before you share</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Managed</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>managed-settings.json</code> and other <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#delivery-mechanisms">managed sources</a></td><td style="text-align:left">Everyone your organization deploys it to; nothing you set overrides it, apart from a few <a class="link" href="#exceptions-to-managed-settings-precedence">security-sensitive exceptions</a></td><td style="text-align:left">Security policy and compliance requirements</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">In the File column, <code>~/.claude</code> is the <code>.claude</code> folder in your home directory, and a bare <code>.claude</code> is the <code>.claude</code> folder inside your project.</span>
<span id="where-each-file-applies"></span>
<span id="compare-what-each-file-reaches"></span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="compare-the-scope-of-each-settings-file"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#compare-the-scope-of-each-settings-file">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Compare the scope of each settings file</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Suppose you have three projects on your machine, <code>website/</code>, <code>api/</code>, and <code>acme-app/</code>, a teammate has their own clone of <code>acme-app/</code>, and you start a <a class="link" href="#settings-in-cloud-sessions">cloud session</a> on <code>acme-app/</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">The graphic below shows which of those folders a setting applies in when you start Claude Code from them. Click a settings file to see the folders it reaches.</span>
<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><strong><code>~/.claude/settings.json</code></strong>: every project on your machine, and nothing on your teammate’s or in the cloud session</li>
<li><strong><code>acme-app/.claude/settings.json</code></strong>: your <code>acme-app/</code>. It reaches your teammate’s clone and the cloud session only if you commit the file to version control; until you do, it’s a file on your disk like any other and nobody else has it</li>
<li><strong><code>acme-app/.claude/settings.local.json</code></strong>: your <code>acme-app/</code> only. Claude Code adds it to your global git excludes the first time it writes the file, so it stays out of your commits; if you create the file by hand, <a class="link" href="#keep-personal-settings-out-of-a-repository">add it to <code>.gitignore</code> yourself</a></li>
<li><strong>Managed settings</strong>, whether a <code>managed-settings.json</code> file, an MDM policy, or <a class="link" href="/docs/en/server-managed-settings">server-managed settings</a> from the claude.ai console: every project on every machine your organization deploys it to, or that you sign in to with your organization account. Only server-managed settings reach the cloud session</li>
</ul>
<span id="which-files-you-have"></span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="find-or-create-your-settings-files"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#find-or-create-your-settings-files">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Find or create your settings files</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Installing Claude Code doesn’t create any settings file. If your machine or project already has one, it came from one of these sources:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Managed</strong>: your organization deploys it. You don’t create or edit it.</li>
<li><strong>Shared project</strong>: a project that already uses Claude Code may have one committed. If not, create it at <code>.claude/settings.json</code> in the project folder.</li>
<li><strong>User</strong> and <strong>Project local</strong>: create them yourself, or let Claude Code create them. It writes <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code> the first time you change an option in the <code>/config</code> menu that it stores in user settings, such as the theme, and <code>.claude/settings.local.json</code> the first time you give a standing approval on a permission prompt, such as “Yes, and don’t ask again” for a Bash command. A few <code>/config</code> options, including <strong>Show tips</strong>, save to <code>.claude/settings.local.json</code> instead of the user file.</li>
</ul>
<div aria-label="Info" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-neutral-200 bg-neutral-50 dark:border-neutral-700 dark:bg-white/10" data-callout-type="info" role="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="flex-none size-5 text-neutral-800 dark:text-neutral-300" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M 7.2 0 C 3.2231 0 0 3.2231 0 7.2 C 0 11.1768 3.2231 14.4 7.2 14.4 C 11.1768 14.4 14.4 11.1768 14.4 7.2 C 14.4 3.2231 11.1768 0 7.2 0 Z M 7.2 13.05 C 3.9741 13.05 1.35 10.4257 1.35 7.2 C 1.35 3.9743 3.9741 1.35 7.2 1.35 C 10.426 1.35 13.05 3.9743 13.05 7.2 C 13.05 10.4257 10.426 13.05 7.2 13.05 Z M 8.325 9.45 H 7.875 V 6.975 C 7.875 6.6038 7.5741 6.3 7.2 6.3 H 6.3 C 5.9288 6.3 5.625 6.6038 5.625 6.975 C 5.625 7.3462 5.9288 7.65 6.3 7.65 H 6.525 V 9.45 H 6.075 C 5.7038 9.45 5.4 9.7538 5.4 10.125 C 5.4 10.4962 5.7038 10.8 6.075 10.8 H 8.325 C 8.6977 10.8 9 10.4977 9 10.125 C 9 9.7523 8.6991 9.45 8.325 9.45 Z M 7.2 5.4 C 7.697 5.4 8.1 4.997 8.1 4.5 C 8.1 4.003 7.697 3.6 7.2 3.6 C 6.703 3.6 6.3 4.0022 6.3 4.5 C 6.3 4.9978 6.7022 5.4 7.2 5.4 Z" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-neutral-800 dark:text-neutral-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">On Windows, <code>~/.claude</code> means <code>%USERPROFILE%\.claude</code>. To keep the home-directory files somewhere else, set <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars"><code>CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR</code></a>; Claude Code then stores your settings, session history, and plugins there instead.</span></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code also keeps a fifth file, <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-directory#ce-claude-json"><code>~/.claude.json</code></a>, that it writes for itself; you don’t need to edit it. It holds your sign-in session, <a class="link" href="/docs/en/mcp">MCP server</a> configurations, per-project state such as trust decisions, and the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-reference#global-config-settings">global config keys</a> that <code>/config</code> writes for you.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="share-settings-with-your-team"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#share-settings-with-your-team">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Share settings with your team</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Commit <code>.claude/settings.json</code> so everyone who clones the repository gets the same permissions, hooks, telemetry, and plugins. Each teammate can still override it for themselves in their own <code>.claude/settings.local.json</code>, so personal exceptions don’t need a commit. For a complete team file, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-example#a-teams-shared-settings">a team’s shared settings</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Some of what you commit waits until each teammate <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#project-allow-rules-and-workspace-trust">trusts the folder</a>, and a few keys never take effect from a repository file; <a class="link" href="#common-cases">Troubleshoot a setting that doesn’t apply</a> covers both.</span>
<span id="local-settings-file"></span>
<span id="where-claude-code-saves-the-project-local-file"></span>
<span id="the-project-local-file"></span>
<span id="keep-personal-settings-out-of-the-repository"></span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="keep-personal-settings-out-of-a-repository"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#keep-personal-settings-out-of-a-repository">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Keep personal settings out of a repository</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">To change a setting for yourself in one project without changing it for your teammates, save it in <code>.claude/settings.local.json</code> inside the project. Claude Code applies that file over the committed <code>.claude/settings.json</code>, so if your team’s file sets <code>"model": "claude-sonnet-5"</code> and you want Opus, put <code>"model": "claude-opus-4-8"</code> in your local file and only your sessions change.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code also writes to this file, keeps it out of your commits, and applies its allow rules without the trust step:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Claude Code writes it too.</strong> When Claude asks permission to run a Bash command and you choose “Yes, and don’t ask again”, Claude Code saves that <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#permission-system">permission approval</a> here as an <code>allow</code> rule.</li>
<li><strong>You don’t need to gitignore it yourself, unless you created it by hand.</strong> The first time Claude Code writes the file in a git repository that doesn’t already ignore it, it adds <code>**/.claude/settings.local.json</code> to your global git excludes file, so the file stays out of your commits in every repository. That file is <code>core.excludesFile</code> when your global git config sets it to an absolute or <code>~</code>-prefixed path; otherwise it’s <code>$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore</code>, or <code>~/.config/git/ignore</code> when <code>XDG_CONFIG_HOME</code> is unset. If you created the file by hand and Claude Code hasn’t written to it yet, add it to <code>.gitignore</code> yourself.</li>
<li><strong>Its allow rules don’t wait for trust while the file stays untracked.</strong> Because the file is yours and not the repository’s, Claude Code applies its <code>allow</code> rules without the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#project-allow-rules-and-workspace-trust">workspace trust</a> step it requires for the committed file. If the file is tracked by git, the trust step applies to it too; see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#when-your-local-settings-file-needs-trust">When your local settings file needs trust</a>.</li>
</ul>
<span id="where-claude-code-looks-for-each-file"></span>
<span id="how-claude-code-keeps-the-local-file-out-of-git"></span>
<span id="local-allow-rules-dont-wait-for-workspace-trust"></span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="where-claude-code-keeps-the-local-file-in-a-git-repository"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#where-claude-code-keeps-the-local-file-in-a-git-repository">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Where Claude Code keeps the local file in a git repository</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">When Claude asks permission to run a Bash command and you choose “Yes, and don’t ask again”, Claude Code saves that approval as an <code>allow</code> rule in <code>.claude/settings.local.json</code>. If you start Claude Code in a subdirectory of a git repository, it reads and writes that file at the repository root and applies the approval across the whole repository. In a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/worktrees">worktree</a>, it uses the file at the main checkout’s root.</span>
<span data-as="p">Two rules qualify the root location:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>When the file stays with <code>.claude/settings.json</code> instead</strong>: outside a git repository, when the repository root is your home directory, on Windows, or when the repository root or its <code>.git</code> or <code>.claude</code> entry isn’t owned by your user.</li>
<li><strong>Paths in the file don’t anchor at the repository root</strong>: a permission rule that starts with <code>/</code> or a relative sandbox path <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#read-and-edit">anchors at the session’s primary working directory</a> instead.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Before v2.1.211, Claude Code kept the file in the starting directory. It still reads a file an earlier version left there alongside the root file; where both set the same key, the root’s value applies, and permission rules from both files apply. The Agent SDK’s <a class="link" href="/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#resolvesettings"><code>resolveSettings()</code></a> helper always reads the file from the starting directory.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code reads the shared <code>.claude/settings.json</code> from the session’s <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#working-directories">primary working directory</a>, so to use a file committed at the repository root, start Claude Code there. After you <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#move-the-session-to-another-directory">move the session with <code>/cd</code></a>, Claude Code reads both project files from the new directory instead, placing the local file by the same rules. Reading them from the directory you moved to requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later.</span>
<span id="managed-settings-delivery"></span>
<span id="precedence-within-the-managed-tier"></span>
<span id="parent-settings-from-embedding-hosts"></span>
<span id="enforce-settings-for-an-organization"></span>
<span id="settings-your-organization-manages"></span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="check-what-your-organization-enforces"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#check-what-your-organization-enforces">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Check what your organization enforces</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">If your organization manages Claude Code, some settings are decided for you and nothing you put in your own files changes them. To see which, run <code>/status</code>: the <code>Setting sources</code> line names the managed source that applies to you. Managed settings apply wherever Claude Code runs on this machine; <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#what-a-developer-can-change">What a developer can change</a> covers local admin rights and tools other than Claude Code.</span>
<span data-as="p">Managed settings reach you through the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#delivery-mechanisms">delivery mechanisms</a> on the managed settings page, most commonly:</span>
<ul>
<li><a class="link" href="/docs/en/server-managed-settings">Server-managed settings</a>, which Claude Code fetches from the claude.ai admin console or a self-hosted <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway">Claude apps gateway</a></li>
<li>MDM or OS-level policies, and <code>managed-settings.json</code> files in a system directory</li>
<li>An embedding host such as Claude Desktop, through the SDK <code>managedSettings</code> option; see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#parent-settings-from-embedding-hosts">Control policy from an embedding host</a></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">In a <a class="link" href="https://claude.com/docs/cowork/overview" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Cowork</a> session that runs on your machine in the Claude Desktop app, Claude Code doesn’t fetch server-managed settings from the claude.ai admin console, and it reads policy deployed to your device unless your organization’s Claude Desktop configuration sets <code>requireCoworkFullVmSandbox</code>. <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#where-and-when-a-policy-applies">Where and when a policy applies</a> covers Cowork and cloud sessions.</span>
<span data-as="p">If you’re the administrator, <a class="link" href="/docs/en/admin-setup">Set up Claude Code for your organization</a> walks through choosing what to enforce, and <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings">Deploy managed settings</a> covers delivery and how to confirm a policy is in force.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="change-a-setting"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#change-a-setting">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Change a setting</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">You can change a setting from the <code>/config</code> menu, by editing a settings file, or for one session from the command line.</span>
<span id="system-prompt"></span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code’s system prompt isn’t published. To give Claude standing instructions, use <a class="link" href="/docs/en/memory"><code>CLAUDE.md</code> files</a> or the <code>--append-system-prompt</code> flag.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="use-the-/config-menu"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#use-the-/config-menu">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Use the /config menu</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Run <code>/config</code> inside Claude Code and open the <strong>Config</strong> tab. It lists a short set of personal options such as theme, editor mode, and verbose output, not every settings key. Select an option to change it; Claude Code saves it for you:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Most options</strong>: <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code></li>
<li><strong>A few options, such as Show tips</strong>: <code>.claude/settings.local.json</code></li>
<li><strong>The <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-reference#global-config-settings">global config options</a></strong>: <code>~/.claude.json</code></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">To set one option without the menu, pass <code>key=value</code>, such as <code>/config verbose=true</code>.</span>
<div aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note" role="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="1.5" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path clip-rule="evenodd" d="M 9 1.6714 C 13.0371 1.6714 16.3286 4.9629 16.3286 9 C 16.3286 13.0371 13.0371 16.3286 9 16.3286 C 7.0574 16.3252 5.1953 15.552 3.8217 14.1783 C 2.448 12.8047 1.6748 10.9426 1.6714 9 C 1.6714 4.9629 4.9629 1.6714 9 1.6714 Z M 9 0 C 4.0371 0 0 4.0371 0 9 C 0 13.9629 4.0371 18 9 18 C 13.9629 18 18 13.9629 18 9 C 18 4.0371 13.9629 0 9 0 Z M 10.2857 3.8571 H 7.7143 V 10.2857 H 10.2857 V 3.8571 Z M 10.2857 11.5714 H 7.7143 V 14.1429 H 10.2857 V 11.5714 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-rule="evenodd" stroke="none"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p"><code>/config</code> is part of the terminal interface. The <a class="link" href="/docs/en/vs-code">VS Code</a> chat panel and the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop">desktop app</a> don’t open it; change settings there by editing a settings file or through those apps’ own settings.</span></div></div>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="edit-a-settings-file"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#edit-a-settings-file">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Edit a settings file</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Open the settings file for the scope you want in your editor and add or change a key. Settings files are strict JSON: a <code>//</code> comment or a trailing comma is a syntax error, and Claude Code reports the file as a <a class="link" href="#fix-a-broken-settings-file">Settings Error</a> at the next start. For example, to let Claude Code run your lint and test commands without asking and stop it reading <code>.env</code> files, add this to <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>:</span>

<span data-as="p">Each entry under <code>permissions</code> is a rule that names a tool and what it may do; <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions">Configure permissions</a> explains the syntax. The <code>$schema</code> line points to the <a class="link" href="https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">published JSON schema</a> for Claude Code settings, which gives you autocomplete and inline validation in VS Code, Cursor, and any other editor that supports JSON schema. The schema can lag behind the newest CLI releases, so a validation warning on a recently documented key doesn’t mean your configuration is invalid.</span>
<span data-as="p">After you save, run <code>/status</code> inside Claude Code to confirm the file loaded; <a class="link" href="#check-what-loaded">Confirm what loaded</a> says what the <code>Setting sources</code> line shows and how a broken file is reported.</span>
<span data-as="p">For a complete personal file, team file, and organization file, each shown with a comment on every key it sets, see the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-example">example settings files</a>.</span>
<span id="pass-settings-for-one-session"></span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="change-a-setting-for-one-session"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#change-a-setting-for-one-session">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Change a setting for one session</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">To try a value without saving it, set it when you start Claude Code. The value applies to that session and your settings files stay as they were. You have three ways to do it:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>--settings</code></strong>: pass a key as JSON, inline or as a path to a file. Claude Code applies it above your user, project, and local files and below managed settings. It can set any key your user settings file can set; it can’t set <code>Managed</code> or <code>Global config</code> keys.</li>
<li><strong>A flag for that key</strong>: some keys have their own flag, such as <code>--model</code> for <code>model</code> and <code>--effort</code> for <code>effortLevel</code> and <code>modelSettings</code>.</li>
<li><strong>An environment variable</strong>: export the key’s paired variable before you run <code>claude</code>, such as <code>ANTHROPIC_MODEL</code> for <code>model</code>.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Each key’s entry on the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-reference">settings reference</a> lists its per-session overrides and which one takes precedence, so check the entry for the key you want to change.</span>
<span data-as="p">Commands you run inside a session mostly save your choice: when you change a setting in <code>/config</code>, Claude Code writes it to your settings files, and <code>/model</code> saves the value as your default for new sessions.</span>
<span data-as="p">If you press <code>s</code> in the <code>/model</code> picker, Claude Code switches the model without saving it as your user default. <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level">Adjust effort level</a> says which <code>/effort</code> picks Claude Code saves as your default for the model you’re using and which apply to the current session only.</span>
<span data-as="p">For example, to start one session on Opus without changing your default:</span>
<div class="code-block mt-5 mb-8 not-prose rounded-2xl relative group min-w-0 print:print-color-exact text-gray-950 dark:text-gray-50 codeblock-light border border-gray-950/10 dark:border-white/10
